subject: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance
messages:
From: Maya Ramirez <m.ramirez@acmecorp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance

Hi Laura,

We saw the notice about the maintenance window you ran over the weekend (refs: Friday alert and Saturday mitigation). Our compliance team asked us to confirm whether any customer data integrity or unauthorized access concerns could have affected our account. Specifically:

- Were any read or write operations retried or rolled back for Acme Analytics during the 03:00–04:15 UTC window?
- Did you observe any unusual egress activity or API keys used outside our normal patterns?

We need a short confirmation for our internal risk team and the SOC intake form so we can close the ticket on our end. If possible, please include pointers to the logs/artifacts you examined.

Thanks,
Maya Ramirez
Security Liaison
Acme Analytics

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramirez <m.ramirez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance

Hi Maya — thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption over the weekend. I want to be transparent and give you our preliminary findings while we complete the full post-incident review.

Summary (preliminary):
- Scope: Maintenance window touched routing and autoscaling for a subset of Dedicated nodes serving region us-west-2. A buggy health-check rollback caused brief task churn between 03:07–03:32 UTC.
- Customer impact: We confirmed no customer payloads were returned to any unknown external IPs and no unauthorized API credentials were used for Acme Analytics.
- Data integrity: We ran checks across the affected shards and compared application-level write checkpoints and object-store ETags. No mismatched checksums or missing sequence numbers were detected for objects attributed to Acme Analytics.

Artifacts/logs reviewed (attached excerpt and evidence form):
- Egress gateway access logs (filtered to Acme Analytics account id)
- API audit trail (token usage, IPs, timestamps)
- Object-store access logs and ETag reconciliation output
- Service orchestration events for the 03:00–04:30 UTC window

Attachments: redwood_incident_log_excerpt_20260811.txt (log excerpts, redacted), acme_evidence_request_form.pdf

Notes and caveats:
- We cannot share raw customer payloads in attachments; instead we provide metadata (timestamps, request ids, hashes) and the excerpts attached.
- Our runs included replays of write confirmations and hash comparisons; while preliminary, these checks are consistent with no data loss or exfiltration affecting your account. We will finalize the postmortem with a signed attestation.

Next steps:
- Markus and Monica are running a second-pass integrity sweep (checksums by shard) and will follow up with the detailed technical artifact if anything changes.
- I will prepare a formal attestation and the post-incident report by EOD.

If you need any specific queries run (IPs, request-ids, exact object keys) reply with a short list and we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0142

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Maya Ramirez <m.ramirez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance

Adding the engineering perspective — ran the integrity passes and a short summary of the checks we executed:

What we ran (technical):
- Replayed application write confirmations against the durability ledger for Acme Analytics (request_ids filtered). All write confirmations that reached the ledger matched object ETags in the object store.
- Per-shard checksum comparison: computed SHA256 over stored payloads (metadata-only comparison for customer privacy) and compared to stored proof-hashes generated at write time; no mismatches.
- KV-cache reconciliation: rehydrated hot caches and cross-checked sequence numbers for the affected deployment slice. No missing sequence gaps observed.
- Egress analysis: aggregated egress by destination IP and ASN; traffic profile matched baseline for your account, and no anomalous external destinations were observed.

Evidence references we placed in the secure drive: folder path (shared link sent below) includes:
- checksum-report-acme-20260811.csv (hash list, masked object ids)
- egress-summary-acme-20260811.json (IP buckets and byte counts)
- orchestration-events-03-04z.log

We did find two retries on a control-plane endpoint due to a transient health-check race; those retries were internal and did not cause duplicate writes.

If you want us to run any additional per-key validations or to provide the exact request-id list for your audit team (redacted payloads), we can produce that and push into the secure folder for download.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramirez <m.ramirez@acmecorp.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance

Maya — following Markus's technical pass we prepared a short attestation for Acme Analytics and uploaded it to the secure folder. The attestation is a formal statement of the checks run and preliminary conclusions and is suitable for your SOC intake.

Attachment: incident_attestation_acme_20260811.pdf (we will also provide a countersigned copy when postmortem is complete).

Secure artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-incident-20260811 (access is restricted to acme@acmecorp.com and the Redwood security/CS team).

We plan a full post-incident review on Thursday 2026-08-13 at 09:00 PT; if you’d like to join the customer-facing portion, I can send a calendar invite.

Thanks for the quick coordination — we take incidents like this seriously and appreciate the partnership on verification steps.

Regards,
Laura

From: Maya Ramirez <m.ramirez@acmecorp.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-08-11T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Impact confirmation request — Saturday maintenance

Laura, Markus — thank you both for the quick and detailed response. The attestation and logs in the secure folder are sufficient for our SOC intake for now. We may request the per-key request-id list later today for our internal audit, but this is great.

Please go ahead and send the calendar invite for the customer-facing portion of the post-incident review on Thursday. If anything material changes in your final postmortem, let us know and we will reopen the ticket.

Best,
Maya Ramirez
Security Liaison
Acme Analytics
